stem: A patient has transient monocular visual loss from an embolus in the retinal circulation. Imaging identifies an ipsilateral neck-artery plaque as its source. Which artery most directly feeds the ophthalmic artery?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Its usual branches supply the face and scalp; the ophthalmic artery normally arises from the internal carotid.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It contributes to the posterior cerebral circulation through the basilar artery, not the usual ophthalmic origin.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This external-carotid branch supplies superficial facial tissues rather than being the normal ophthalmic origin.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The ophthalmic artery usually arises from it; the central retinal artery then branches from the ophthalmic artery.

options.label: E
options.explanation: This external-carotid branch supplies deep pharyngeal and skull-base structures rather than the usual ophthalmic origin.

context: The usual arterial route is internal carotid to ophthalmic to central retinal artery. This explains why carotid disease can produce visual symptoms in one eye.
